title: Model-index schema + onboarding playbook for variant pinning and perf profile publishing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and roll out a definitive 'model-index' metadata schema and an onboarding playbook that supports explicit variant pinning, hardware affinity hints, and automated performance-profile publication into the model catalog and docs portal.

Background:
- Recent onboarding work exposed gaps: inconsistent variant naming, missing hardware affinity tags, and ad-hoc perf measurements that make automatic rollouts fragile.
- We need a compact, backward-compatible metadata schema used by ingestion pipelines, the Console model page, and the runtime for deterministic pinning.

Scope / Deliverables:
1) model-index schema v1 (JSON-schema text snippet added to catalog repo) with fields: model_id, semantic_version, variant_tag, lineage_parent, quantization_profile, hardware_affinity (list), seq_length_profile, perf_profile_id, compatibility matrix (runtime versions), and doc_link.
2) Onboarding playbook: step-by-step doc (Confluence + README) for engineers and SEs covering: selection of benchmark workloads, quantization labels, publishing perf runs, and pinning strategies (exact version vs. semantic minor pin).
3) Ingestion changes: validation hook in model-catalog CI that enforces schema and rejects missing perf_profile_id or hardware_affinity for shippable variants.
4) Console/docs updates: expose pinning UI guidance on the model detail page and auto-link published perf profiles.
5) Perf-profile auto-publish: wire the perf pipeline to create perf_profile objects and tag them in the catalog (perf job -> perf_profile_id -> publish event).
6) Migration script: small caret-preserving migration for existing catalog entries without breaking runtime compatibility.

Acceptance criteria:
- model-index schema merged to model-catalog repo with unit tests and examples.
- Onboarding playbook published at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Model+Index+Playbook and a short README in the repo.
- CI validation added: PRs that add models must pass schema validation or provide exemptions documented in the playbook.
- Console shows the perf_profile link and an explicit 'Pin to model-index' button in the model detail page (design handoff in PR).
- Two new models onboarded using the playbook as a pilot with perf profiles published and runtime pinning successful in the staging cluster.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Strict schema validation will slow down ad-hoc adoptions; mitigated by an exemptions flow and a lightweight "draft" flag.
- Perf-profile generation can add infra cost; we'll limit auto-benchmark runs for initial pilot and warn customers in docs.

Open questions:
- Do we require perf_profile_id for every variant or only for those marked 'shippable'? Proposed: require for shippable variants only.
- Definition of "hardware_affinity" vocabulary (gpu-family v.s. gpu-generation). Action: agree on controlled vocab in kickoff.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: schema design and playbook draft, alignment meeting with Console and QA (owners: Marco, Priya).
- Week 2: schema PR, CI validator, migration script, initial perf pipeline hook (owner: infra team).
- Week 3: Console UI copy + link, test pilot onboarding of 2 models, address feedback.
- Week 4: finalize docs, merge, and announce in eng weekly.

- Perf pipeline proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-runner/pull/1180
